# Book III, Proposition 1

*The centre of a given circle*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> To find the centre of a given circle.

**In Lean:** ✅ proved, as Euclid states it · Euclid's argument

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/01-idea.svg" alt="Halve any straight line drawn across the circle (red), draw another (blue) across the circle through its middle at right angles (yellow), and halve that one too: its middle is the centre." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>Halve any straight line drawn across the circle (red), draw another (blue) across the circle through its middle at right angles (yellow), and halve that one too: its middle is the centre.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/01.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.1, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC be the given circle;

thus it is required to find the centre of the circle ABC.

Let a straight line AB be drawn through it at random, and let it be bisected at the point D;

from D let DC be drawn at right angles to AB and let it be drawn through to E;

let CE be bisected at F;

I say that F is the centre of the circle ABC.

For suppose it is not, but, if possible, let G be the centre,

and let GA, GD, GB be joined.

Then, since AD is equal to DB,

and DG is common,

the two sides AD, DG are equal to the two sides BD, DG respectively;

and the base GA is equal to the base GB, for they are radii;

therefore the angle ADG is equal to the angle GDB. [I. 8]

But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right; [I. Def. 10]

therefore the angle GDB is right.

But the angle FDB is also right;

therefore the angle FDB is equal to the angle GDB, the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore G is not the centre of the circle ABC.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other point except F.

Therefore the point F is the centre of the circle ABC.

<a name="porism"></a>PORISM. From this it is manifest that, if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line into two equal parts and at right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting straight line.

Q. E. F.

Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out. The list below marks where a lemma does a step Euclid takes for granted, where several sentences share one step, where the Lean takes a case Euclid's figure leaves aside and where a porism is proved as a theorem of its own; the `/- … -/` notes in the listing explain smaller adjustments.

**How the Lean follows the text**

- **A further case, by `Prop1.middle`.** "and let GA, GD, GB be joined." Euclid's figure keeps the supposed centre G off AB. On AB it would be AB's middle point D, which is already on CE, so the Lean sets that case aside first; then DAG and DBG are triangles for I.8.
- **Done by `Prop1.perpendicular`.** "But the angle FDB is also right…" If AB passes through the centre, F is D and there is no angle FDB, so the Lean takes the angle CDB, right by construction. For "the greater to the less" it shows that at D only one straight line is at right angles to DB, wherever G lies, so G is on CE.
- **Carried together.** "Therefore G is not the centre of the circle ABC." The reductio shows that the supposed centre G lies on CE, and the Lean beneath makes it the middle point F. One argument, for any centre G, carries all three sentences.
- **Proved separately, as `Prop1.porism`.** "PORISM. From this it is manifest…" Proved as its own theorem, III.1 Por., from this construction. It uses that a circle has one centre (`centre_unique`), which III.1 itself does not.

/-- A straight line has one middle point. Euclid takes this for granted when he
identifies the centre on CE with its middle point F. -/
theorem Prop1.middle {A B D G : Point} (hADB : Between A D B) (hAD : ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖)
    (hAGB : Between A G B) (hAG : ‖A G‖ = ‖G B‖) : G = D := by
  have e₁ := len_add_of_between hAGB
  have e₂ := len_add_of_between hADB
  rw [← hAG] at e₁
  rw [← hAD] at e₂
  have hlen : ‖A G‖ = ‖A D‖ := Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (e₁.trans e₂.symm)
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hADB)
  have hray : OnRay G A D := ⟨ne_of_between hADB, (ne_of_between hAGB).symm,
    ⟨L, hA_L, on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_L hB_L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA_L hB_L⟩,
    fun hb => not_between_of_between hAGB (between_of_between_right hb hADB)⟩
  exact OnRay.eq_of_len_eq hray hlen

/-- At a point A of the straight line AD, only one straight line is at right
angles to it. Euclid takes this for granted in "the greater to the less". With E
and F on one side of AD, the equal right angles put F on AE; on opposite
sides, EA produced beyond A makes a right angle on F's side. -/
theorem Prop1.perpendicular {A D E F : Point} (hE : Triangle D A E) (hF : Triangle D A F)
    (hDAE : ∠ D A E = ∟) (hDAF : ∠ D A F = ∟) : Collinear A E F := by
  have hAD : A ≠ D := hE.ne₁₂.symm
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hD_L⟩ := Postulate1 A D hAD
  have hE_L : ¬ OnLine E L := hE.bac.off_line hA_L hD_L
  have hF_L : ¬ OnLine F L := hF.bac.off_line hA_L hD_L
  by_cases hs : SameSide F E L
  · exact (onRay_of_angle_eq (SameSideOf.of_line hAD hA_L hD_L hs) (hDAF.trans hDAE.symm)).2.2.1
  · obtain ⟨M, hE_M, hA_M⟩ := Postulate1 E A hE.ne₂₃.symm
    obtain ⟨E', hE'_M, hEAE', -⟩ := Postulate2 hE_M hA_M hE.ne₂₃.symm []
    have hD_M : ¬ OnLine D M := fun hD => hE ⟨M, hD, hA_M, hE_M⟩
    have hEAD : ∠ E A D = ∟ := by rw [angle_symm hE.ne₂₃.symm hE.ne₁₂]; exact hDAE
    have hDAE' : ∠ D A E' = ∟ := (adjacent_eq_of_right hE_M hE'_M hEAE' hD_M hEAD).symm.trans hEAD
    have hE'_L : ¬ OnLine E' L := fun h => hE_L (on_line_of_between (between_symm hEAE') h hA_L)
    have hFE' : SameSide F E' L := same_side_of_opposite_sides
      ⟨hE_L, hF_L, fun h => hs (same_side_symm h)⟩ ⟨hE_L, hE'_L, pasch3 hEAE' hA_L⟩
    obtain ⟨-, -, ⟨N, hA_N, hE'_N, hF_N⟩, -⟩ :=
      onRay_of_angle_eq (SameSideOf.of_line hAD hA_L hD_L hFE') (hDAF.trans hDAE'.symm)
    have hNM : N = M := line_unique (ne_of_between (between_symm hEAE')).symm hA_N hE'_N hA_M hE'_M
    subst hNM
    exact ⟨N, hA_N, hE_M, hF_N⟩

```lean
/-- To find the centre of a given circle. -/
theorem Prop1 {A B : Point} {ABC : Circle} (hABC : ∃ G : Point, Centre G ABC) (hA : OnCircle A ABC)
    (hB : OnCircle B ABC) (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ F C D E : Point, Centre F ABC ∧ Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖ ∧ OnCircle C ABC ∧
      OnCircle E ABC ∧ Between C D E ∧ ∠ A D C = ∟ ∧ Between C F E ∧ ‖C F‖ = ‖F E‖ := by
  -- Let ABC be the given circle;
  -- thus it is required to find the centre of the circle ABC.
  -- Let a straight line AB be drawn through it at random, and let it be bisected at the point
  -- D;
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  obtain ⟨D, hADB, hAD⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hAB
  have hD_L := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_L hB_L
  -- from D let DC be drawn at right angles to AB and let it be drawn through to E;
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, -⟩ := exists_off_line hAB []
  obtain ⟨X, hXQ, hX⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hAB ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L, hD_L⟩ hQ
  have hD_in : InsideCircle D ABC := inside_of_between (Or.inr hA) (Or.inr hB) hADB
  have hX_L : ¬ OnLine X L := hXQ.triangle.off_line hA_L hB_L
  have hDX : D ≠ X := fun e => hX_L (e ▸ hD_L)
  obtain ⟨N, hD_N, hX_N⟩ := Postulate1 D X hDX
  obtain ⟨E, hE, hE_N, hEDX⟩ := line_circle_beyond hD_in hD_N hX_N hDX.symm
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hC_N, hCDE⟩ := line_circle_beyond hD_in hD_N hE_N (ne_of_between hEDX)
  have hCray : OnRay C D X := OnRay.of_between_between hEDX (between_symm hCDE)
  have hDA : D ≠ A := (ne_of_between hADB).symm
  have hDB : D ≠ B := (ne_of_between (between_symm hADB)).symm
  have hADC : ∠ A D C = ∟ := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right hCray hDA.symm]
    exact hX A ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L, hA_L⟩ hDA.symm
  have hCD : C ≠ D := ne_of_between hCDE
  have hC_L : ¬ OnLine C L := fun h => hX_L ((line_unique hCD hC_N hD_N h hD_L) ▸ hX_N)
  -- let CE be bisected at F;
  obtain ⟨F, hCFE, hCF⟩ := BookI.Prop10 (ne_of_between_ends hCDE)
  -- I say that F is the centre of the circle ABC.
  -- For suppose it is not, but, if possible, let G be the centre,
  obtain ⟨G, hG⟩ := hABC
  have hG_N : OnLine G N := by
    refine Classical.byContradiction fun hG_N => ?_
    -- and let GA, GD, GB be joined.
    /- A centre on AB would be its middle point D, already on CE. We set that case aside, so
       that DAG and DBG are triangles for I.8. -/
    have hG_L : ¬ OnLine G L := fun hG_L =>
      hG_N ((Prop1.middle hADB hAD
        (between_of_inside_chord hG_L hA_L hB_L (centre_inside hG) hA hB hAB)
        (by rw [len_symm A G, Definition15 hG hA hB])) ▸ hD_N)
    have hDAG : Triangle D A G := Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hDA hG_L
    have hDBG : Triangle D B G := Triangle.of_line hD_L hB_L hDB hG_L
    -- Then, since AD is equal to DB,
    have hDA_DB : ‖D A‖ = ‖D B‖ := by rw [len_symm D A, hAD]
    -- and DG is common,
    have hDG : ‖D G‖ = ‖D G‖ := rfl
    -- the two sides AD, DG are equal to the two sides BD, DG respectively;
    -- and the base GA is equal to the base GB, for they are radii;
    have hGA_GB : ‖G A‖ = ‖G B‖ := Definition15 hG hA hB
    -- therefore the angle ADG is equal to the angle GDB. [I. 8]
    have h8 : ∠ A D G = ∠ G D B :=
      (BookI.Prop8 hDAG hDBG hDA_DB hDG (by rw [len_symm A G, len_symm B G, hGA_GB])).trans
        (angle_symm hDBG.ne₁₂.symm hDBG.ne₁₃.symm)
    -- But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one
    -- another, each of the equal angles is right; [I. Def. 10]
    /- Definition I.10 makes each of the equal adjacent angles right, and Postulate 4
       makes it `∟`, as in I.11. -/
    have hADG : ∠ A D G = ∟ := Postulate4 ⟨B, hADB, hDAG.bac, h8⟩
    -- therefore the angle GDB is right.
    have hGDB : ∠ G D B = ∟ := h8 ▸ hADG
    -- But the angle FDB is also right;
    /- If AB passes through the centre, F is D and there is no angle FDB. We take in its
       place the angle CDB, right by construction. -/
    have hBDC : ∠ B D C = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_onRay_right hCray hDB.symm]
      exact hX B ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L, hB_L⟩ hDB.symm
    -- therefore the angle FDB is equal to the angle GDB, the greater to the less: which is
    -- impossible.
    have hDBC : Triangle D B C := Triangle.of_line hD_L hB_L hDB hC_L
    obtain ⟨M, hD_M, hC_M, hG_M⟩ := Prop1.perpendicular hDBC.bac hDBG.bac hBDC
      ((angle_symm hDBG.ne₁₂.symm hDBG.ne₁₃.symm).trans hGDB)
    exact hG_N ((line_unique hCD hC_M hD_M hC_N hD_N) ▸ hG_M)
  -- Therefore G is not the centre of the circle ABC.
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other point except F.
  -- Therefore the point F is the centre of the circle ABC.
  /- The centre is within the circle, hence between C and E. Its equal radii
     make it the middle point F, the step Heath says Euclid takes for granted
     (vol. 2, p. 8). -/
  have hCGE := between_of_inside_chord hG_N hC_N hE_N (centre_inside hG) hC hE
    (ne_of_between_ends hCDE)
  obtain rfl : G = F := Prop1.middle hCFE hCF hCGE (by rw [len_symm C G, Definition15 hG hC hE])
  exact ⟨G, C, D, E, hG, hADB, hAD, hC, hE, hCDE, hADC, hCFE, hCF⟩
  -- PORISM. From this it is manifest that, if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line
  -- into two equal parts and at right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting
  -- straight line.
  /- The consequence is proved from this construction in `Prop1.porism` below. -/
  -- Q. E. F.
```

```lean
/-- The Porism to III.1: "if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line into two
equal parts and at right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting straight
line." The straight line DC cuts AB, a straight line in the circle, at its
middle point D and at right angles, and the centre G is on DC. III.9 and III.10
cite it. -/
theorem Prop1.porism {A B C D G : Point} {ABC : Circle} (hG : Centre G ABC) (hA : OnCircle A ABC)
    (hB : OnCircle B ABC) (hADB : Between A D B) (hAD : ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) (hADC : ∠ A D C = ∟) :
    Collinear D C G := by
  obtain ⟨F, C', D', E', hF, hAD'B, hAD', -, -, hC'D'E', hAD'C', hC'FE', -⟩ :=
    Prop1 ⟨G, hG⟩ hA hB (ne_of_between_ends hADB)
  have hD'D : D' = D := Prop1.middle hADB hAD hAD'B hAD'
  have hFG : F = G := centre_unique hF hG
  rw [hD'D] at hC'D'E' hAD'C'
  rw [hFG] at hC'FE'
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hADB)
  have hD_L := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_L hB_L
  have hDA : D ≠ A := (ne_of_between hADB).symm
  have hC_L : ¬ OnLine C L := (show Triangle A B C from hC).off_line hA_L hB_L
  obtain ⟨N, hC'_N, hE'_N⟩ := Postulate1 C' E' (ne_of_between_ends hC'D'E')
  have hD_N := on_line_of_between_ends hC'D'E' hC'_N hE'_N
  have hG_N := on_line_of_between_ends hC'FE' hC'_N hE'_N
  have hC'D : C' ≠ D := ne_of_between hC'D'E'
  by_cases hGD : G = D
  · subst hGD
    obtain ⟨M, h1, h2⟩ := Postulate1 G C (fun e => hC_L (e ▸ hD_L))
    exact ⟨M, h1, h2, h1⟩
  have hC'_L : ¬ OnLine C' L := by
    intro h
    have hNL : N = L := line_unique hC'D hC'_N hD_N h hD_L
    have hG_L : OnLine G L := hNL ▸ hG_N
    exact hGD (Prop1.middle hADB hAD
      (between_of_inside_chord hG_L hA_L hB_L (centre_inside hG) hA hB (ne_of_between_ends hADB))
      (by rw [len_symm A G, Definition15 hG hA hB]))
  have hDAC : Triangle D A C := Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hDA hC_L
  have hDAC' : Triangle D A C' := Triangle.of_line hD_L hA_L hDA hC'_L
  obtain ⟨M, hD_M, hC'_M, hC_M⟩ := Prop1.perpendicular hDAC'.bac hDAC.bac hAD'C' hADC
  have hMN : M = N := line_unique hC'D hC'_M hD_M hC'_N hD_N
  subst hMN
  exact ⟨M, hD_M, hC_M, hG_N⟩
```

</details>

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74) (used here): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between A and C. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70) (used here): If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between A and D. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L155) (used here): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43) (used here): If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35) (used here): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`centre_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L32) (porism): A circle has only one centre. (Generalities 2)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201) (used here): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26) (used here): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between B and C. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L46): Let a point be taken on the other side of L from B. (Points 6)
- [`exists_point_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L42) (used here): Let a point be taken on the same side of L as B. (Points 5)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L38) (used here): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161) (used here): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, heading out to a point C outside it, cuts the circle between B and C. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75) (used here): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28) (used here): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of L crosses L. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49) (used here): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52) (used here): If B is between A and C, then A is not between B and C. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79) (used here): If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92) (used here): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56) (used here): A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes through C. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61) (used here): A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114) (used here): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99) (used here): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89) (used here): If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side as A. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A. If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139) (used here): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L67) (used here): A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4)
- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54) (used here): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (used here): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17) (used here): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21) (used here): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49) (used here): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle ABC can be applied to the straight line L with A on D, B on the ray from D through G, and C on the side of L where H is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45) (used here): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35) (used here): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (used here): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (used here): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

**Where must the centre lie?** Book III opens by finding the point so many of its proofs will need. Euclid bisects AB at D and draws DC at right angles to it, and the centre must lie on that straight line; bisecting CE then picks it out. Book I's two tools, the bisection and the right angle, are all it takes.

**"Nothing more to base the proof upon."** Why construct F and then argue that no other point G can be the centre? Robert Simson observed that the proof could only be by *reductio ad absurdum*, and Heath explains why: "At the beginning of Book III. we have nothing more to base the proof upon than the definition of a circle, and this cannot be made use of unless we assume some point to be the centre" (vol. 2, p. 8). In our foundations too a circle has a centre only when a hypothesis gives one, so we state III.1 for a circle that has some centre, Euclid's G, and prove that the point F it constructs is that centre.

**"Taken for granted rather than proved."** Isaac Todhunter observes that D is taken to be within the circle, which Euclid proves only in III.2, and Heath that the straight line through D must meet the circle twice, which nothing before it ensures (vol. 2, p. 7). And at the end, "It is however taken for granted rather than proved that the centre must be the middle point of CE" (Heath, vol. 2, p. 8). All three are settled here: the rules System E calls Circle 2 and Intersections 5 put D within the circle and find C and E, and `Prop1.middle` proves that a straight line has one middle point.

**"The greater to the less."** In Euclid's figure the centre is off AB, the angle FDB is right, and GDB is a part of it. But if AB passes through the centre, F falls on D and there is no angle FDB at all. So we set the right angle CDB beside GDB, and `Prop1.perpendicular` says what "the greater to the less" stands for: at D only one straight line is at right angles to DB, wherever G lies. The Porism then follows from the construction, as Euclid says it does.

**The modern way.** The points p as far from a as from b satisfy 2p·(b − a) = |b|² − |a|², the perpendicular bisector of AB, and the centre o is one of them. That line meets the circle of radius r at o ± ru, for a unit vector u along it, and their midpoint is o.

## Further reading

- For why the centre can be proved only indirectly, since "no direct Demonstration can be given of it", Robert Simson's [*The Elements of Euclid*](https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_elements-english-sele_euclid_1756_0) (1756, free online), the note "Prop. I. B. III." (p. 363), in the Glasgow first edition whose notes Heath quotes again and again.
- For the whole of Book III as a mathematician reads it today, Benno Artmann's [*Euclid: The Creation of Mathematics*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-1412-0) (1999), the chapter "Euclid Book III: About the Circle", a walk through the book in today's language.
